disclaimer: All values are typical figures from general engineering knowledge, given as min-max ranges to reflect grade, process and supplier variation. Every record is flagged 'typical-value-needs-verification' and must be spot-checked against supplier datasheets or a handbook before the results are relied on.

materials.name: PLA
materials.notes: Easy to print and stiff for a polymer, but brittle and softens near 55 C; poor in a hot, crash-prone airframe.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PLA+ (toughened PLA)
materials.notes: PLA with impact modifiers: a little tougher than plain PLA but still limited by low temperature capability.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PETG
materials.notes: Tougher and more heat tolerant than PLA; a common all-round printing material.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: ABS
materials.notes: Light and reasonably tough with good heat tolerance; prone to warping when printed.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: ASA
materials.notes: Like ABS but resists sunlight and weather better, useful for outdoor airframes.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: Nylon PA12
materials.notes: Tough, fatigue-resistant and low-friction; absorbs little moisture compared with other nylons.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: Nylon PA6
materials.notes: Strong and tough but absorbs moisture, which lowers stiffness in humid air.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: TPU 95A (flexible)
materials.notes: Rubber-like and extremely impact tolerant, but far too floppy for load-carrying structure; useful for bumpers and mounts.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: Polycarbonate (PC)
materials.notes: Very tough and heat tolerant; harder to print and needs a hot, enclosed printer.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PC-ABS blend
materials.notes: Blend of polycarbonate and ABS: tougher than ABS, easier to print than pure PC.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: Polypropylene (PP)
materials.notes: Very light and chemically resistant but soft and difficult to bond or print well.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PEEK
materials.notes: Excellent heat and chemical resistance and good strength, but very expensive and needs specialist printers.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PEI (ULTEM-type)
materials.notes: High-temperature, flame-retardant engineering polymer; costly and needs specialist printers.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, typical FDM settings; cost is filament/stock price per kg.

materials.name: PLA-CF (carbon-filled PLA)
materials.notes: PLA with chopped carbon fibre: much stiffer than plain PLA but brittle and still limited by temperature.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: PETG-CF
materials.notes: PETG with chopped carbon fibre: stiffer and easier to print than nylon composites.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: ABS-CF
materials.notes: ABS with chopped carbon fibre: light, stiff and heat tolerant but still warps when printed.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: PA-CF (carbon-filled nylon)
materials.notes: Nylon with chopped carbon fibre: a popular strong, light and heat-resistant printed structural choice.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: PA-GF (glass-filled nylon)
materials.notes: Nylon with glass fibre: cheaper than carbon-filled nylon, slightly heavier and less stiff.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: PC-CF (carbon-filled polycarbonate)
materials.notes: Carbon-filled polycarbonate: stiff and heat tolerant; needs a hot enclosed printer.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: PEEK-CF
materials.notes: Top-end printable composite for heat and strength, at very high cost and with specialist equipment.
materials.property_basis: Short-fibre-filled filament printed in XY (in-plane) orientation; fibre fraction typical of commercial filaments; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy (quasi-isotropic laminate)
materials.notes: Benchmark for light, stiff structure; expensive, energy intensive and hard to recycle.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Carbon/epoxy (woven 0/90 laminate)
materials.notes: Carbon fabric laminate loaded along its fibre directions; slightly stiffer than quasi-isotropic in those directions.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Glass/epoxy (woven laminate)
materials.notes: Cheaper and tougher than carbon but heavier and less stiff; a common budget composite.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Aramid/epoxy (woven laminate)
materials.notes: Aramid (Kevlar-type) fibres absorb impact very well; weaker in compression and hard to cut.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Basalt/epoxy (woven laminate)
materials.notes: Volcanic-rock fibre composite, between glass and carbon in stiffness at a modest price.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Flax/epoxy (woven laminate)
materials.caveat: Moisture uptake and batch variation of natural fibres are not modelled.
materials.notes: Plant-fibre composite with good vibration damping and a lower fibre footprint; limited strength and moisture sensitive.
materials.property_basis: Laminate at roughly 50% fibre volume, in-plane properties of a quasi-isotropic or balanced woven layup (not unidirectional); cost is raw laminate material per kg.

materials.name: Hemp-PLA (moulded biocomposite)
materials.caveat: Moisture uptake and low heat tolerance are not modelled beyond the temperature figure; fibre content varies by supplier.
materials.notes: Bio-based composite of hemp fibre in PLA, hot-pressed or moulded; eco-friendly but low heat tolerance.
materials.property_basis: Compression-moulded or injection-moulded sheet with roughly 30% hemp fibre, in-plane values (random mat); not a printed filament.

materials.name: Aluminium 6061-T6
materials.notes: Everyday aerospace aluminium: easy to machine, weld and recycle; the usual metal baseline.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Aluminium 7075-T6
materials.notes: High-strength aluminium for highly loaded parts; less corrosion resistant and loses strength with heat.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Aluminium 5052-H32 (sheet)
materials.notes: Formable sheet aluminium that bends easily for brackets and skins; lower strength than 6061.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Titanium Ti-6Al-4V
materials.notes: Very strong and corrosion resistant but expensive and costly to machine and produce.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Magnesium AZ31
materials.notes: The lightest structural metal; flammable as chips, corrodes easily and needs coating.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Stainless steel 304
materials.notes: Tough, corrosion-proof and cheap, but very dense; mostly used for fasteners and small fittings.
materials.property_basis: Wrought material, isotropic, in the temper named; cost is stock price per kg.

materials.name: Balsa wood
materials.caveat: Moisture uptake, grain direction and density variation between sheets are not modelled; wood needs sealing and careful joints.
materials.notes: Classic ultra-light hobby aircraft wood: great stiffness for its weight but crushes easily and absorbs moisture.
materials.property_basis: Along-grain values for grades from about 100 to 200 kg/m3; strong grain-direction dependence.

materials.name: Birch plywood (aircraft/hobby grade)
materials.caveat: Moisture uptake, grain direction and glue quality are not modelled; values apply along the face grain only.
materials.notes: Cheap, easy to cut and glue; much heavier than balsa but far tougher.
materials.property_basis: Typical values along the stronger in-plane/grain direction for the density grade stated; foams use compressive modulus as the stiffness figure.

materials.name: Bamboo laminate
materials.caveat: Moisture uptake, grain direction and adhesive quality are not modelled; values apply along the fibre direction only.
materials.notes: Fast-growing renewable material with high strength for a natural product; moisture sensitive.
materials.property_basis: Typical values along the stronger in-plane/grain direction for the density grade stated; foams use compressive modulus as the stiffness figure.

materials.name: Agglomerated cork sheet
materials.caveat: Very soft: usable as a damping or padding layer, not as primary structure.
materials.notes: Soft, light and good at absorbing vibration and impact; offers almost no structural stiffness.
materials.property_basis: Typical values along the stronger in-plane/grain direction for the density grade stated; foams use compressive modulus as the stiffness figure.

materials.name: EPP foam
materials.notes: Springy foam that survives crashes by bouncing back; the standard for hand-launched and combat foam aircraft.
materials.property_basis: Bulk foam; compressive modulus used as stiffness; strength is the typical tensile or compressive figure.

materials.name: EPS foam
materials.notes: Very light and cheap but crumbles on impact; often used as a skin-covered wing core.
materials.property_basis: Bulk foam; compressive modulus used as stiffness; strength is the typical tensile or compressive figure.

materials.name: XPS foam board
materials.notes: Smooth, rigid foam board popular for cheap foam-board aircraft; dents and cracks easily.
materials.property_basis: Bulk foam; compressive modulus used as stiffness; strength is the typical tensile or compressive figure.

materials.name: PET structural foam core
materials.notes: Closed-cell foam used as the core between composite skins; recyclable thermoplastic.
materials.property_basis: Bulk core foam; compressive modulus used as stiffness; only meaningful as a sandwich core.

materials.name: Aluminium honeycomb core
materials.notes: Hexagonal-cell aluminium core for stiff, light sandwich panels; costly and only useful bonded between skins.
materials.property_basis: Effective out-of-plane (through-thickness) compressive properties of the core; only meaningful as a sandwich core.

materials.name: Aerogel-core panel
materials.caveat: Values are very uncertain; the panel is mainly a thermal barrier and is mechanically fragile.
materials.notes: Thermally insulating panel with a silica-aerogel core; excellent for heat shielding but mechanically weak. Values are very uncertain.
materials.property_basis: Effective panel properties for an aerogel-blanket-cored sandwich; wide ranges reflect high uncertainty.

materials.name: Recycled PET (rPET)
materials.notes: Printing filament made from used bottles or packaging; similar to PETG with a lower embodied-energy footprint.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, recycled-content filament; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: Recycled nylon (rPA)
materials.notes: Nylon filament made from reclaimed material such as used fishing nets; properties vary by batch.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, recycled-content filament; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: Recycled polypropylene (rPP)
materials.notes: Recycled PP filament or pellets: very light and low footprint but soft.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, recycled-content filament; cost is filament price per kg.

materials.name: Recycled PLA (rPLA)
materials.notes: PLA reclaimed from failed prints and offcuts; like virgin PLA with some loss of strength.
materials.property_basis: Printed specimens, XY (in-plane) orientation, recycled-content filament; cost is filament price per kg.
